- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) in recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.4), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the first 5–7 days after a strong positive sentiment event; add 0.5–1.5x the spike magnitude as a buffer.
- Model overestimates price after sharp downward moves; reduce forecast by 1–3% of recent mean for 3–5 days post-drop.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often lag by 1–2 days; if sentiment is trending, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks >10% above recent high, reduce by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
